claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation that forms a CrTaO4-based surface scale will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Ti-V-Nb-Ta is an example of the refractory high-entropy alloy to which the intervention could be applied.
The alloy initially lacks a preformed protective oxide layer.
Pre-oxidation at approximately 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere will induce formation of a dense CrTaO4-based surface oxide.
The CrTaO4-based surface oxide forms rapidly during the pre-oxidation treatment.
The intervention should provide benefits during 1100°C isothermal oxidation for exposures up to 200 hours.
The intervention should work at temperatures above 1100°C.
The intervention produces a dense and continuous CrTaO4-based oxide scale.
The resulting CrTaO4-based scale is adherent.
The preformed CrTaO4-based scale acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
The diffusion barrier minimizes oxygen ingress and oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Suppressing oxygen ingress preserves the alloy's structural integrity at extreme temperature.
Relative to an untreated alloy, a pre-oxidized sample will have significantly lower oxygen uptake and weight gain.
Relative to an untreated alloy, a pre-oxidized sample will develop a more uniform and protective oxide scale.
Direct exposure of an untreated alloy produces less-protective or discontinuous oxide layers, higher oxidation rates, and material degradation.
CrTaO4 is thermodynamically favored around 1100°C under oxygen-rich conditions.
The benefit may not apply at considerably lower temperatures.
The benefit may not apply under atmospheric conditions different from oxygen-rich exposure.

contradictions.description: The illustrative Ti-V-Nb-Ta alloy contains no stated Cr, yet the intervention is supposed to form a CrTaO4-based scale in situ without adding a chromium source.
